subsystems.name: Alloy composition
subsystems.role: the metal mixture itself, chosen so it stays liquid near room temperature and conducts electricity well.
parts: indium and tin added to lower the melting point
optional bismuth or zinc for specific properties

subsystems.name: Native oxide skin
subsystems.role: a nanometers-thin gallium oxide layer that forms instantly in air, letting the liquid hold a shape but also hindering flow.
parts: electrolyte or surfactant for electrochemical control

subsystems.name: Containment and encapsulation
subsystems.role: keeps the liquid metal in place while allowing bending, stretching or reshaping.

subsystems.name: Actuation and control
subsystems.role: moves or reconfigures the liquid metal to change a circuit or drive a soft robot.

subsystems.name: Electrical interfacing
subsystems.role: connects the liquid metal to conventional wires and circuits without creating high-resistance joints.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the metals
buildSteps.detail: High-purity gallium, indium and tin are weighed. Gallium is solid at room temperature but melts in warm water; the others need higher heat.

buildSteps.title: Melt and alloy
buildSteps.detail: The metals are heated together to around 250 °C in an inert atmosphere until fully molten, then stirred to homogenise the mixture.

buildSteps.title: Cool to a eutectic alloy
buildSteps.detail: The melt is cooled slowly. For a gallium–indium–tin eutectic such as Galinstan, the alloy stays liquid well below 0 °C.

buildSteps.title: Shape or inject
buildSteps.detail: The liquid alloy is drawn into microchannels, printed through a fine nozzle, or cast into a mould. The oxide skin that forms in air helps it hold the shape.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate
buildSteps.detail: The channels or printed patterns are sealed inside a silicone elastomer or sandwiched between flexible films.

buildSteps.title: Add electrodes and wiring
buildSteps.detail: Metal wires or conductive pads are inserted at the ends of the liquid metal tracks to connect to external electronics.

buildSteps.title: Activate and test
buildSteps.detail: A voltage or mechanical pressure is applied to move the liquid metal, change its shape, or open and close a circuit; the device is then tested for electrical continuity.

prerequisites.why: gallium is a by-product of aluminium refining; the alloy cannot be made without it.
these metals lower the melting point and are already produced for solders and coatings.
knowing the exact ratios that stay liquid at room temperature is essential for stable alloys.
the native oxide allows shaping but must be managed with electrolytes or surfactants for reliable movement in devices.
these techniques create the fine channels and elastomer structures that hold the liquid metal.

pathway.milestone: gallium-based alloys sold for thermal interfaces, thermometers and lab demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: a reliable supply of the raw material and basic handling know-how.

pathway.milestone: commercial soft robots and stretchable conductors using liquid metal tracks
pathway.unlocks: flexible wiring that survives repeated bending and stretching.

pathway.milestone: reconfigurable antennas and circuits that change shape on demand
pathway.unlocks: devices that can switch function without replacing hardware.

pathway.milestone: self-healing and adaptive electronic skins for wearables and robotics
pathway.unlocks: machines and interfaces that repair themselves after damage.
